item.title: England thrash Croatia 7-0 in UEFA Nations League
item.description: England produced a dominant attacking performance to thrash Croatia 7-0 in their UEFA Nations League Group 3 clash. Harry Kane scored twice while Bukayo Saka also grabbed a double as England delivered an impressive performance under head coach Thomas Tuchel.
item.content:encoded:
England produced a dominant attacking performance to thrash Croatia 7-0 in their UEFA Nations League Group 3 clash.

Harry Kane scored twice while Bukayo Saka also grabbed a double as England delivered an impressive performance under head coach Thomas Tuchel.

Kane opened the scoring in the eighth minute before Jude Bellingham doubled England’s lead in the 21st minute.

Anthony Gordon made it 3-0 in the 39th minute before Saka struck just before half-time to give England a 4-0 lead at the break.

England continued to dominate in the second half as Kane scored his second in the 53rd minute before Saka made it 6-0 in the 68th.

Substitute Morgan Rogers completed the 7-0 victory with a goal in the 87th minute.

Bellingham also played a major role in the victory with three assists.

item.title: Bula Boys claim MSG Cup title after defeating defending champions Vanuatu 1-0
item.description: The Fiji Bula Boys have won the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 after defeating defending champions Vanuatu 1-0 in the final at the HFC Bank Stadium. Thomas Dunn fired Fiji ahead in the 10th minute, sending the home crowd into celebration.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Bula Boys have won the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 after defeating defending champions Vanuatu 1-0 in the final at the HFC Bank Stadium.

Thomas Dunn fired Fiji ahead in the 10th minute, sending the home crowd into celebration.

Fiji took the 1-0 lead into half-time before holding off Vanuatu in the second half to seal the victory and lift the title on home soil.

Meanwhile, Fiji captain Roy Krishna says the Bula Boys were determined to win the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup on home soil after working hard for the opportunity to lift a trophy in front of their home fans.

He also thanked the fans for their support during the tournament and urged them to continue backing the young Fiji team.

He also dedicated the win to the team, his teammate Tevita Warainivalu for his hard work and coach Stephane Auvray.

Fiji Bula Boys coach Stephane Auvray says the team had to change its game plan and become more compact defensively to protect their 1-0 lead against Vanuatu in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup final.

Auvray says Fiji initially tried to play according to their first-half plan, but when they realised it was not working, they switched three players in midfield to become more compact and solid.

He says Fiji could have done better with the chances they created but was pleased the team managed to hold on and secure the victory.

Krishna says the victory is only the beginning for the team and believes the side has a big future under the current coaching setup.

He says the team is young and will need time to develop, but continued support from the fans will be important.

The victory was also sweet revenge for the Bula Boys after Vanuatu defeated Fiji 1-0 during the round-robin stage of this year’s tournament.

item.title: Tailevu draw 18-all with defending champions Malolo
item.description: Tailevu fought back in the final moments to draw 18-all with defending champions Malolo in Round 10 of the Skipper Cup at Nakelo District School Grounds. Kini Douglas converted a crucial penalty at the death to secure the draw for Tailevu.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu fought back in the final moments to draw 18-all with defending champions Malolo in Round 10 of the Skipper Cup at Nakelo District School Grounds.

Kini Douglas converted a crucial penalty at the death to secure the draw for Tailevu.

In other Round 10 results, Naitasiri went down 41–24 to Nadi, after entering the round as the table leaders from Round 9.

In the Skipper Cup U20, Suva beat Taveuni 34–18, while Tailevu defeated Malolo 17–15.

In the Subrails Marama Cup, Tailevu defeated Namosi 38–29, while Nadroga beat Rewa 42–12.

Nadi also recorded a 41–24 win over Naitasiri in the Marama Cup.

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Manchester City appeal guilty verdict over Premier League financial breaches
item.description: Manchester City have lodged an appeal after an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations. The club says the commission's ruling contains what it describes as clear errors of law, principle and fact, and maintains it has evidence supporting its position.
item.content:encoded:
Manchester City have lodged an appeal after an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The club says the commission's ruling contains what it describes as clear errors of law, principle and fact, and maintains it has evidence supporting its position.

City were found guilty of breaching financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The independent panel found that City arranged what it described as sham contracts with several commercial partners to disguise more than FJ$2.46 billion in secret funding.

The Premier League says the club systematically broke its rules for nearly a decade.

Meanwhile, the Football Association says the verdict has significant implications for the integrity of the game and it is considering the decision and what action may be required.

Proceedings between Manchester City and the Premier League remain ongoing.
